summary.headline: Kwality Pharma Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue up 63% YoY to INR181 crore, EBITDA margin 27.5%, FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR720 crore plus.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 63% YoY to INR181 crore in Q2 FY27 from INR111 crore, with PAT doubling to INR29 crore and EBITDA margin at 27.5%. H1 FY27 revenue was INR343 crore. FY27 revenue guidance was raised to INR720 crore plus, with management privately viewing INR720-750 crore as achievable. Management reiterated FY28 potential of INR950-1,000 crore and FY29 of INR1,000 crore, and detailed a large capex and BE-driven pipeline; working capital days improved, though the call also surfaced auditor and secretarial resignations, since replaced by KPMG.

financial_highlights.metric: FY27 PAT guidance (as cited by analyst from PPT)

segments.name: Exports / regulated and LATAM-MENA registrations
segments.commentary: Growth driven mainly by MENA (Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia) and Mexico and Colombia new registrations. Own-registration EBITDA margin cited at 28-32% vs 24-26% when exporting through partners.

segments.name: Biologics (erythropoietin)
segments.commentary: About 1% of Q2 revenue; biowaiver-based sales in Egypt, with revenue expected from Q3 FY27. Management targets INR30-40 crore in FY28 and INR80-100 crore by FY29.

segments.name: Hormones
segments.commentary: Hormone plant expected to commercialise from Q2-Q3 FY28; management sees INR100-150 crore from hormones, not included in INR1,000 crore target.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR720 crore plus; management said INR720-750 crore is achievable.
FY27 EBITDA margin expected at 27-28%; 29-30% possible only if revenue exceeds INR1,000 crore at similar operating costs.
FY28 revenue potential of INR950-1,000 crore; management said above INR1,000 crore is possible with European and Brazilian registrations.
FY29 revenue expected to rise further; 19 BE products to contribute about INR300 crore by FY29, with first seven products giving INR80-90 crore in FY28.
Gross margin expected to fall to 44-46% (cost) with gross margin 54-55% as R&D spend rises from 2.5% to 5-6% of revenue from Q1 FY28.
Capex of roughly INR500-600 crore over three years (Unit 7 INR200-250 crore; BE facilities INR250-300 crore), funded mainly by internal accruals plus bank loans; no equity dilution planned as of now.
US ANDA filing targeted by FY28 for cephalosporin/beta-lactam CDMO-based products, excluded from guidance; visibility expected Q1 FY28.
No split, bonus or dividend planned at present, as earnings are being ploughed into expansion.
capex_capacity: Capex of INR140-150 crore planned before FY27 end is largely done; another INR20-25 crore pending, expected by April 2027.
Unit 7 (four acres acquired) to be built in three phases over FY28-FY30; management indicated INR300 crore revenue from new facility in FY29.
Unit 1 third shift running in oral solids and a few injectable lines (six or seven lines); full third shift needed when revenue nears INR1,000-1,200 crore.
27D licence application for biological fill-to-finish filed with CDSCO; audit completed, licence expected Dec 2026 to Feb 2027, enabling CDMO biologics work.
Facility has capacity for 200 BE products run in batches of 40; BE pipeline target of 200 studies by FY29-30.
demand_pricing: Q2 growth attributed to new registrations in MENA (Algeria, Morocco, Tunisia), Mexico and Colombia; management said prime focus is LATAM and Europe, with less reliance on Middle East after INR60-70 crore of debtors stuck there in Q4 FY26 were realised in Q1 and Q2.
Mexico registrations take 14-18 months and other Latin countries 12-14 months; 19 dossiers ready, 21 more by early 2027.
Raw material: about 85% of procurement from India and 10-15% from China; Indian API prices up about 4-5%, absorbed by mix shift.
Pricing in USD is set in INR terms per management, with currency movements said to be passed through in unit price; management said FX has no material impact.
Erythropoietin: no Indian company registered in Latin, European, African markets per management; Eprex and an Argentinian company cited as competitors.
Biologics: pembrolizumab, nivolumab and pertuzumab biowaiver applications to be filed, with some quantities targeted for March-April 2027.

qa_highlights.question: Is FY29 INR1,000 crore target conservative given growth momentum?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY28 could reach INR950-1,000 crore or more, with 30-35% growth achievable; European and one Brazilian registration could push it above INR1,000 crore in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue ramp from the 19 BE products?
qa_highlights.answer: First seven molecules to give INR80-90 crore in FY28 (South Asia and Latin America); remaining 12-13 products by FY29, taking the total to around INR300 crore from the 19 products.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR720 crore guidance conservative and will H2 seasonality hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called INR720 crore conservative and said INR720-750 crore is achievable; cited KPMG's onboarding, December holidays and international market shutdown until 15 January as reasons for not raising guidance higher.

qa_highlights.question: Who holds registrations for partner-exported revenue and what are margins?
qa_highlights.answer: About 20% of FY28-29 revenue, roughly INR200 crore of the INR1,000 crore, still sits with partner-held MAs, mainly in African or unregulated markets; partner-exported EBITDA margin 24-26% vs 28-32% on own registrations.

qa_highlights.question: Capex and funding over the next few years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated INR500-600 crore capex over three years plus INR60-80 crore extra working capital; funded through internal accruals and some bank loans, with no equity dilution planned now.

qa_highlights.question: Will the ANDA and US FDA plans be disclosed?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a US ANDA for one or two cephalosporin/beta-lactam CDMO-based products is targeted by FY28 but is excluded from guidance; visibility expected in Q1 FY28, subject to audit and acceptance.

qa_highlights.question: Does EBITDA guidance include hormone plant costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said running costs of the hormone plant will hit margins before sales, so FY27 margin guidance is kept at 27-28%; hormone revenue of INR100-150 crore in FY28 would lift margins to 28-29%.

risks_watch: Hormone plant running costs start before commercial sales; margin could fall to 27-28% if hormone revenue of INR100-150 crore slips.
Concentration on regulatory approvals: Mexico, Brazil and Europe registrations, plus biowaiver acceptance for erythropoietin and pembrolizumab, drive FY28-29 numbers.
Auditor and company secretary resignations on the results day, with KPMG appointed as replacement; governance to monitor.
Debtor days still at 178 days; Middle East receivables stuck in Q4 FY26.
Capex and working capital needs of INR500-600 crore over three years rely on bank loans and internal accruals; tax rate in Q2 was higher, sustainable rate not yet provided.
Management acknowledged the company-level biosimilar opportunity is contingent on clinical trials and partner funding.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on pipeline and long-term potential, with repeated caveats that targets are conservative and speculative. Evasive on US ANDA product details, tax rate (deferred to company secretary) and biosimilar revenue timing; several answers stressed uncertainty around regulatory outcomes.
key_quotes: We believe that if we are able to cross INR1,000 or INR1,200 crores mark, we will probably be able to sustain a 30% EBITDA margins.
As of now, there is no such plan for equity dilution.
But we do not want to raise very high expectations.

BE facilities (part of INR500-600 crore three-year capex plan)

growth.why: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR720 crore plus (INR720-750 crore achievable) from INR700 crore, with H1 revenue of INR343 crore and Q2 up 63% YoY; backing comes from new MENA/LATAM registrations, Unit 1 third-shift capacity, and a INR500-600 crore three-year capex plan, but the major capacity (Unit 7, BE facilities) only comes online in FY28-FY30, so near-term support is partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: FY27 EBITDA margin guided at 27-28% (held), 29-30% only if revenue exceeds INR1,000 crore; gross margin falls to 44-46% cost-side and R&D rises from 2.5% to 5-6% of revenue from Q1 FY28, so margins are more likely to compress than expand.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Hormone plant commercialises Q2-Q3 FY28 (INR100-150 crore revenue), BE facilities and Unit 7 (INR200-250 crore) planned over FY28-FY30; INR20-25 crore pending capex due by April 2027, but major new capacity lands mostly after the 2-4 quarter window.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: FY27 revenue guidance raised to INR720 crore plus (INR720-750 crore achievable) from INR700 crore, H1 FY27 at INR343 crore and Q2 up 63% YoY to INR181 crore, driven by MENA, Mexico and Colombia registrations.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: INR500-600 crore three-year capex plan already stated (Unit 7 INR200-250 crore, BE facilities INR250-300 crore), with INR140-150 crore largely done and INR20-25 crore pending by April 2027.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management called the INR720 crore guide conservative with INR720-750 crore achievable, and FY28 could reach INR950-1,000 crore or above, but H2 seasonality, December holidays and a 15 January market shutdown are cited as reasons not to raise further now.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Debtor days still at 178, hormone plant running costs start before sales (margin could fall to 27-28%), and Q2 tax rate was higher with sustainable rate not yet given; auditor and secretary resignations add governance risk.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: First seven BE products to give INR80-90 crore in FY28, biologics (erythropoietin) revenue from Q3 FY27 targeting INR30-40 crore in FY28, hormone plant from Q2-Q3 FY28, and a US ANDA for cephalosporin CDMO products targeted by FY28 (excluded from guidance).

rows.label: LATAM and Europe registrations (Mexico, Colombia, Brazil, Europe)
rows.why: Mexico registrations take 14-18 months and other Latin countries 12-14 months; 19 dossiers ready with 21 more by early 2027, and one European plus one Brazilian registration could push FY28 above INR1,000 crore.

rows.label: CDMO biologics via 27D licence (fill-to-finish)
rows.why: 27D licence application filed with CDSCO and audit complete, licence expected Dec 2026 to Feb 2027, but biosimilar revenue depends on clinical trials and partner funding, which management was evasive on.

rows.label: Debtor days reduction from 208 to 178
rows.why: Working capital cycle fell from 170 to 130 days and debtor days from 208 to 178 after INR60-70 crore of stuck Middle East receivables were realised, but 178 days is still high and FY28-29 growth needs INR60-80 crore extra working capital.

tone.note: Management was confident on FY27 guidance upgrade, FY28 INR950-1,000 crore potential and the BE/LATAM pipeline, but evasive on US ANDA product details, tax rate and biosimilar revenue timing; analysts pushed on FY29 target conservatism and H2 seasonality.

oneOffs.what: INR60-70 crore of Middle East debtors stuck since Q4 FY26 were realised in Q1 and Q2 FY27; cash collection, not stated as revenue, so effect on reported revenue growth is unclear

quality.why: Consolidated revenue rose 63% YoY to INR181 crore from INR111 crore, with growth attributed to new MENA, Mexico and Colombia registrations (a volume/new-customer driver), but the brief gives no volume percentage and does not state a one-off revenue gain; the receivable recoveries are cash items and the brief does not say they lifted reported revenue.
